text: Write a program that uses short-circuit evaluation to make an otherwise unsafe expression safe. Fill in the two blanks.
choices: System.out.println(___);         // safe: uses the short-circuiting operator
System.out.println(___);     // unsafe: uses the eager operator
explanation: Verified: the first prints false and the second throws `/ by zero`. `&&` evaluates its right side only if the left is true; `&` always evaluates both. So short-circuiting is not an optimisation, it is a control-flow construct that changes which code runs — which is exactly why Chapter 25 shows it cannot be written as an ordinary method: a method's arguments are all evaluated before the call.
